item.title: Over 13,000 dog licences issued in Kerry up to end of November last year
item.description: Over 13,000 (13,151) dog licences were issued in Kerry between January and the end of November last year. Figures compiled by Kerry County Council, show that 44 fines relating to dogs were issued during the same period. The council also rehomed 74 dogs between January and the end of November last year. Advertisement The previous year, the council issued over 15,500 dog licences in Kerry and 140 dogs were rehomed in Kerry during all of 2024.

item.title: Cathaoirleach of Kerry County Council to unveil Cystic Fibrosis exhibition
item.description: The Cathaoirleach of Kerry County Council will be unveiling the Kerry leg of an exhibition highlighting the social and economic challenges faced by people living with Cystic Fibrosis. Cystic Fibrosis, of CF, is a genetic respiratory disorder that causes chronic breathing issues, persistent lung infections, poor nutrient absorption, and digestive problems. item.title: Minister says job losses at Abbeyfeale KOSTAL show Ireland must focus on competitiveness
item.description: The approximately 140 job losses announced at KOSTAL in Abbeyfeale show that Ireland must focus on its manufacturing competitiveness. That's according to the minister for tourism and media, Patrick O'Donovan from West Limerick. He was speaking in the wake of KOSTAL's announcement that it will move the production of on-board EV chargers from its Abbeyfeale plant to China, potentially in the last quarter of this year. item.title: Kerry County Councillor says taskforce recommending local authorities have more power is positive
item.description: A Kerry County Councillor says the findings of a Government taskforce which recommends that more powers should be given to local authorities is positive. The local democracy taskforce is due to report to the Government in the coming weeks. The Irish Examiner reports that the Association of Irish Local Government (AILG) has seen some recommendations in the taskforce's final report. item.title: Ward added to Irish squad
item.description: Ireland have added Bryn Ward to their squad ahead of Saturday’s Six Nations meeting with Italy at the Aviva Stadium. The Ulster back row joins the group as Tadhg Furlong continues his return to full fitness, having resumed full training. Ireland trained at Clongowes Wood College today with no new injury concerns, and a final decision on Furlong’s availability will be made before Thursday’s team announcement. item.title: Udogie likely to be out for remainder of the season
item.description: Tottenham could be without Destiny Udogie for the rest of the season. He's suffered a hamstring injury and faces another spell out, having only recently returned to action. The 23 year old was forced to come off in the defeat to Manchester United, and could be out for five weeks. Advertisement Manager Thomas Frank also said today, Kevin Danso and Dejan Kulusevski remain weeks away from a return from injury.

item.title: Kerry secondary school to receive new special education class for upcoming academic year
item.description: A secondary school in Kerry will receive a new special education class. It’s part of 41 additional classes nationwide sanctioned by the Department of Education for the 2026/27 academic year. Pobalscoil Inbhear Scéine in Kenmare has been included in the latest tranche of schools. Advertisement It brings to 17 the number of special classes approved for Kerry in 2026, and 301 nationally. item.title: No space in detention centre for Kerry teen facing burglary charges
item.description: A Kerry teenager facing a spate of burglary charges has been told he would be in custody only for there being no beds available at Oberstown Detention Centre. The 15-year-old boy, who cannot be named as he is a minor, appeared before Judge David Waters at Tralee District Court. The teen faces 29 charges in relation to separate incidents of burglary and theft in the county.
